takeaways.label: 19% growth, structurally higher baseline
takeaways.text: Revenue growth hit 19%, driven by a deliberate margin-accretive product mix shift and broad-based traction across every segment; management calls it "clear empirical proof" of a transition beyond cyclical automotive demand.

takeaways.label: Industrial and CV segments surged
takeaways.text: The commercial vehicle segment grew 47% and the industrial segment grew 48%, both powered by new technologies, new product launches, and deeper co-engineering partnerships with global tier one OEMs.

takeaways.label: Margins protected, PAT optics dismissed
takeaways.text: EBITDA grew much faster than revenues in H1, and management explicitly urged investors to ignore profit after tax because depreciation is rising as new capacities come online; the focus must be on operating EBITDA and EBITDA margin.

takeaways.label: Aerospace and Unitec JV are the next legs
takeaways.text: The Mahant Tool Room acquisition added AS9100D certification and mission-critical defense supply; the Unitec JV is on track for April 2027 commissioning, though management declined to provide any FY28 revenue breakup.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether the promised six-month capacity-driven growth upswing materializes, any aerospace customer announcements, and whether the 17–18% EBITDA margin floor holds as depreciation continues to climb.

points.label: Broad-based expansion
points.text: Growth occurred in every segment: two-and-three wheelers, passenger cars, commercial vehicles, farm equipment (including LCV, MCV, HCV), industrial, and exports, which returned to a 16%+ growth trajectory.

points.label: Mix-driven, not volume-chasing
points.text: The company deliberately pivots away from commoditized products (e.g., in two-wheelers) toward differentiated high-margin products and does not grow at the expense of margin.

points.label: Capacity-led upswing ahead
points.text: Within the next six months, the company expects to move to a higher growth trajectory as new capacities start coming online; management framed this as a visible step-change every six months, not a quarterly blip.

points.label: Export momentum building
points.text: Export growth will keep moving up, supported by expanding pipelines and deeper engagements with global tier one OEMs.

points.label: COGS discipline
points.text: Cost of goods sold rose only ~1% due to extremely efficient cost management, waste elimination, and product mix response, even as other expenses rose 19% on power, fuel, logistics, and input costs.

points.label: Receivables health
points.text: Customer receivables DSO remained flat despite high growth, which management considers "extremely healthy" because DSO typically rises in high-growth periods.

quotes.text: Harshbeena Zaveri: "Is 19% growth sustainable? Definitely. Once we reach a new threshold of growth, we definitely intend to sustain and surpass it."

points.label: Mahant Tool Room traction
points.text: Q2 actual sales of ₹55 lakh exceeded targets; the business is moving toward a turnover of ₹1 crore per quarter, which will take another 9 months to a year, but when target customers come in, "it will jump at ₹10 crores at a time."

points.label: Certification base complete
points.text: MTR holds all required certifications, including AS9100D, and has additionally received certification for bearings that go into aerospace applications.

points.label: Current defense supply
points.text: MTR already supplies the most critical applications (landing gears, doors) for prestigious defense aircraft like Sukhoi.

points.label: Long gestation, sticky wins
points.text: Aerospace and defense business has a long acquisition period, minimum 18 months for bearings, but "once you get it, you have the business forever."

points.label: Partnerships-driven model
points.text: The company buys "access and speed, not capacity" and only acquires capabilities, not customers and capacities; global clients who had reached out to build aerospace capabilities will be announced as engagements materialize.

points.label: Competitive moat in customization
points.text: Peers have traditionally been strong in high-volume manufacturing, while NRB is strong in customized manufacturing solutions, a structural advantage as the world needs more customized bearing solutions, including in aerospace.

quotes.text: Harshbeena Zaveri: "We buy access and speed, not capacity. We firmly believe that the kind of capacities that we create, which is why we are partnerships-driven and not, in the real sense, M&A-driven, where you actually go and acquire customers and you acquire capacities. We only acquire capabilities."

points.label: Commissioning on track
points.text: The Unitec JV at Aurangabad is on track for commissioning by April 2027, focused on broad industrial applications with a heavy focus on industrial gearboxes.

points.label: Customer anchor
points.text: One customer for whom capacity is being put in place has recently listed on the stock exchanges.

points.label: Ramp will be gradual
points.text: Full capacity utilization of the ₹130 crores revenue potential will not happen in FY28 itself; management stated "that's not the way capacities for an entirely new business division are led."

points.label: Revenue breakup withheld
points.text: Management declined to provide any FY28 revenue breakup for the JV, stating that all breakups are given only at the consolidated level.

points.label: Capacity philosophy
points.text: The company adds capacity only on orders that are already firmly in place, establishing a higher operational baseline with each expansion.

points.label: EBITDA outperformance
points.text: EBITDA grew much faster than revenues for H1, per an analyst's math that management did not dispute.

points.label: Margin floor commitment
points.text: The company "definitely like[s] to maintain our EBITDA as a percentage of sales," previously stated as a 17–18% ratio.

points.label: Depreciation distortion
points.text: Management urged investors to stop looking at profit after tax because depreciation is kicking in as new capacities come online; the correct comparison is operating EBITDA and EBITDA as a percentage of sales.

points.label: Other expenses pressure
points.text: Other expenses rose 19% YoY driven by power, fuel, logistics, and input cost impacts; management expects to offset these with higher growth as capacity builds.

points.label: Annual performance floor
points.text: Once the company achieves something, "it does not fall below it, at least on an annual basis."

quotes.text: Harshbeena Zaveri: "That is the reason why our profit after tax is not a correct measure. Because the depreciation is kicking in. You have to compare us for apples to apples with other companies, which is both actually operating EBITDA and EBITDA as a percentage of sales, which is where we are shining and outperforming."

sections.title: Strategic Vision: Five Verticals, One Decade

points.label: Five verticals reiterated
points.text: Aerospace (buying speed, not scale); Automotive adjacency (moving beyond legacy products into tapered and ball bearings, wheel hubs, spherical roller bearings); EV beyond electrification (high-frequency drives, commercial EV fleets, e-two-wheelers, off-highway e-mobility); Mobility beyond vehicles (robotics, AGVs, urban air mobility, advanced automated transit systems); Mission-critical friction solutions (stationary and mobile).

points.label: Decade-shaping decisions
points.text: Decisions being taken today are designed to shape NRB over the next decade; the substantial pivot will lead to "an entirely different NRB."

points.label: Five-year vision
points.text: Build a differentiated business vertical in segments where technical complexity, customer stickiness, and credibility matter.

points.label: Talent strategy
points.text: The company gives 20–30% salary jumps to internal people filling vacancies rather than losing its best people to competitors at 30–40% higher salaries.

quotes.text: Harshbeena Zaveri: "I am a conservative person when it comes to commitment. You have to always take everything I say with a pinch of salt. We like to over-perform and under-promise. It is part of our company conservative financial approach."

items.title: ₹2,500 crore FY31 revenue goal
items.text: Management targets ₹2,500 crore revenue by FY31 (12-13% CAGR), and as of Q1 FY27 said the target "looks like lower than we're going to achieve," with the aspirational vision at ₹3,000 crore as new verticals add in. That implies roughly doubling today's ~₹1,456 crore revenue base, with aerospace and industrial bearings carrying the incremental growth.

items.title: Aerospace via Mahant Tool Room
items.text: NRB completed the ₹27.5 crore acquisition of Mahant Tool Room on 17 Jul 2026, gaining AS9100D certification, a ₹30 crore order book that is 100% HAL, and a designed-with-HAL-Nashik Sukhoi-30 plain spherical bearing fewer than five companies worldwide can make. Management targets ₹300 crore aerospace revenue by 2031 with ~30% EBITDA margins at that scale, with the current ₹20 crore trajectory potentially reaching ₹100 crore next year.

items.title: Unitec JV cylindrical roller bearings
items.text: The JV with Unitec S.r.L./Mondial (NRB ≥75%, ₹67 crore NRB investment) is on track to commission at Aurangabad by April 2027, with Unitec committed to buying back 20% of annual output and its customers including Bonfiglioli, SAME and Leonardo. The ₹110 crore capex supports ₹130 crore of turnover, opening industrial gearbox and European OEM business NRB does not have today.

items.title: ₹270 crore brownfield capacity expansion
items.text: The Board-sanctioned ₹270 crore programme (₹200 crore Apr 2025, ₹70 crore Feb 2026, ₹40 crore land May 2026) lifts capacity 15-25%, with ₹60 crore spent and ₹100 crore ordered as of Q1 FY27; commissioning runs from June-July 2026 through Q1 2028. With effective utilisation near full across plants, management's rule of thumb - ₹100 crore capex yields ₹130 crore of sales - points to roughly ₹350 crore of added revenue potential.

items.title: Industrial bearings scale-up
items.text: Industrial friction solutions grew 48% YoY in Q2 FY27 and now stand at 14-15% of revenue, with a new Siemens win and a target of 20-25% of revenue in about three years at margins in line with the 18-21% goal. Import-substitution JVs with global players, backed by the BIS push, could take the company beyond ₹2,500 crore.

items.title: Make-in-USA and global nominations
items.text: Lifetime nominated business rose from ₹800 crore to ₹1,100 crore after the Q1 FY27 General Motors Corvette planet-pins win - the first for the Columbia, South Carolina plant, on a program open only to US manufacturers. FY27 international growth is guided at 10-14% versus 4% in FY26, with new BMW steering business starting from January.
